label: sec:nucleon-derivation-intro
html: The linear programming machinery selects the Borromean operator \mathcal{B}_3 as the unique confinement optimum. We apply this selection rule to the photon pair-production vertex to derive the nucleons. Closing the four-term photon braid with \mathcal{B}_3 yields the proton and neutron normal forms. These normal forms remain independent of the incoming photon polarization. We package this construction as the derived atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N). This completes the derivation chain \gamma\gamma \to q\bar q \to \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n} \to \mathcal{A}(Z, N), establishing the foundation for our subsequent study of nuclear stability.
